title: Second app bundles and the duplicated policy text
why: Two of these rows are second full applications, but they are not the same problem. `maya-os-site/index.html` (S-240) is the real duplicate: a 2.5 MB near-duplicate of `app.html` carrying the same twelve widgets, the same dispatcher and the same onboarding quick-reply handling — two copies of the primary interface mean every contract edit must land twice or the surfaces diverge in behaviour. `сайт и приложение/app-tenant.html` (S-667, 1.1 MB) is a second application too, but not a second copy of that system: it has no widget system (`grep -c meRenderWidgetCard` = 0), no client consent path (`grep -c` = 0) and no governed settings (`grep -c` = 0). For that file what is being approved is not the deletion of a copy but the construction — in the generator that produces it — of a system that was never built there: different cost, different risk. The third row, `privacy.html` (S-657), is not a bundle at all: it is a fourth divergent wording of the policy text — alongside `privacy_policy.py` PRIVACY_TEXT, `webhook_server` `_PRIVACY_SHORT` and the maya-os-site rendering — and it is unreachable today, while the bot's own policy presentation implies a public policy URL that does not exist.
disappear: The MAYA OS site bundle stops being a second rendering site of the widget system — the one place in this group where two copies of the same system are collapsed into one, and a diff-and-prove job rather than a delete. `app-tenant.html` stops being a separately maintained second application, but it folds into the generator (`saas_blueprint/pg/tenantize_frontend.py`), not into `app.html` by deletion. `privacy.html` stops being a fourth divergent wording of the policy. None of it happens now: the work sits in package K5/K8, and every row carries the same retirement condition — RETIRE AFTER PARITY at K16.
remain: White-labelling remains, as configuration driven through the generator rather than as a second checked-in bundle. `/app/tenant-test.html` remains resolvable — it is live today, so it must keep working through a redirect rather than vanishing with the file. The policy remains as content: one canonical wording with a real public URL, with every channel pointed at it. All three rows stay in place until parity is proven, and the surface each one folds into is still unnamed (REQUIRES SIGNATURE) — naming those targets is what the signature decides.
risk: MEDIUM-HIGH for the work, though the signature itself executes nothing. Two copies of the primary interface are the single largest tax on any chat-first change, and merging them means diffing two multi-megabyte generated bundles and proving behavioural equality — they are near-duplicates rather than verified-identical copies, with line offsets differing throughout. CLAUDE.md gotcha #2 removes the safety net: the Aurora sources do not exist, so the merge operates on generated output with no build to regenerate it from, and a bad merge is not recoverable by rebuilding. Two hazards sit behind the MERGE label: `app-tenant.html` is generated (`saas_blueprint/pg/tenantize_frontend.py:180`), so the merge target is the generator and any edit to the output bundle is overwritten on the next tenantize run; and `/app/tenant-test.html` is a live URL, so a path change without a redirect costs a tenant their app. The work sits in package K5/K8 and the merge targets are still to be named — this row records the decision, not the execution.
user_impact: Two of the three bundles are live and both have users who notice; only one row is genuinely invisible. (a) S-667 `app-tenant.html` is deployed at `/app/tenant-test.html`, but `saas_blueprint/CUTOVER_RUNBOOK.md` §0.3 defines it as a "тестовый фронт ОТДЕЛЬНЫМ файлом" whose rollback is deleting the file — a smoke-test front for the operator, not a client channel; the no-redirect hazard is real, but the people holding the link are testers, not clients. Its missing widget system (`grep -c meRenderWidgetCard` = 0 vs 2 in app.html) and missing governed settings are not a merge gap: the file is generated from app.html by `saas_blueprint/pg/tenantize_frontend.py` and is simply a stale generation (`__ME_SAAS_CTX` = 0 occurrences vs 150 in app.html), so re-running the generator restores those screens. The merge is not what "gives" them the widget chat. (b) S-240 `maya-os-site/index.html` is NOT invisible to every user. It is the same single-file app at build stamp `2026-08-01-crm-analytics-v2`, and `maya-saas-backend/deploy/platform/build-mayaos-edge.sh` copies it verbatim to the edge root `index.html`. Its own sibling rows say so: S-761 calls its push block "LIVE… a working notification control from a live tenant"; S-646 calls it "the ONLY live PWA that shows a client any policy text before they accept" (`setPrivacy(d.privacy_text || '')`, L22078); S-618 records `?consent` and `?device_id` deep links that only it carries. The implementation envelope's G10 exit criterion — "`maya-os-site/index.html` unreachable, probe recorded" (K15) — is the target state, not today's. Collapsing this bundle is visible: unless `privacy_text` rendering (grep: 1 there, 0 in app.html) and the `?consent` force-show are ported first, its users lose the policy screen they see today. (c) S-657 `privacy.html` is the one row where "nobody notices" holds — verified unreachable, the only repo reference is its own L4 self-instruction. But the successor wording "privacy.html becomes the served policy text the consent widget already reads" is false today: app.html's AMayaConsent renders no policy text at all (`privacy_text` grep = 0); the widget has to be taught to read it, and the file has to actually be published.
security_impact: Not an improvement in consent-record consistency — that part is neutral — and a real capability check is at risk. (1) There is one consent writer today, not two. `webhook_server.py:4796 consent_submit_handler` is an A18 initiator that performs no local write; `legacy_client_command_bridge.py` states "No phone/User resolution, local consent write, or mutating fallback" and forwards to `http://127.0.0.1:3107/api/internal/legacy/client-commands/consent` — the same NestJS Client-consent boundary app.html reaches directly via `/client-channel/consent` (`customers.controller.ts:74 submitLegacyNativeConsent`). The merge collapses two transports, not two record paths, so "net improvement in consent-record consistency" overstates a neutral change. (2) The duplicates' legacy submit is dead, not redundant: `package5-client-consent-proxy.php` requires a string `idempotency_key` for `consent_submit` and rejects with 400 otherwise, and neither duplicate sends one (`idempotency_key`/`idempotencyKey` = 0 in app-tenant.html; S-646 records the same dead-submit defect for maya-os-site). Both bundles therefore present a blocking 152-ФЗ gate whose signature cannot be recorded — a live compliance defect that the merge would fix. That is the real security gain, and it should be named as a defect rather than as "consistency". (3) "All three carry the same legacy AConsentGate" is false: in app.html it is retired to `function AConsentGate() { return null; }` ("Retired legacy consent presentation. Only AMayaConsent is mounted below."), while in both duplicates it is a live blocking screen posting to `CONSENT_PROXY = 'https://malesthetic.pro/app/api-proxy.php'`. (4) A check IS removed unless the merge direction is inverted. S-646: merging onto AMayaConsent, which shows no policy text, is "a straight downgrade in legal presentation… the single clearest instance in the cluster of a merge destroying capability"; S-618: an app.html-canonical merge "silently drops the 152-FZ consent force-show AND the `?device_id` reader". "No authority check is lost" is true only in the narrow sense that authority is server-side; stated as "no check removed" it is a false all-clear. (5) Tenant isolation is unchanged by the decision, as claimed — though both duplicates hardcode the salon proxy and the bridge pins `externalCompanyId` to the single configured `YCLIENTS_COMPANY_ID` ("binds the configured tenant, never the consenting Client"), so a white-label tenant's consent is already recorded against the configured tenant; the merge neither creates nor fixes that. No frozen limitation is contradicted by this corrected text; the original contradicted G10 by treating a K15 exit criterion as present-day fact.
